Markets let you define audiences using conditions and tailor their experience with customizations, including currency, language, pricing, and theme content.
Discounts and gift cards work across markets, but fixed-amount values are converted between currencies at checkout.
You can use Markets to sell to customers in different countries and regions from a single store.
Markets group countries, regions, or customer segments into audiences that receive a tailored shopping experience.
After your markets are active, you can create, edit, activate, deactivate, and delete markets as your business grows.

identifier: Overview of markets features and concepts
statement: Each market represents a set of customers, such as those in a particular region, and the customizations you apply to that market determine what experience those customers get when they visit your store.

Conditions: Conditions define who your market applies to. Conditions can be countries and regions for cross-border selling, company locations for B2B, retail locations for selling in person, or sales channels for selling across channels.
If a customer doesn't match any of your active markets when browsing the online store, then the experience that they get is that of your backup region instead.
Create markets for countries and regions to sell across borders. You can group countries together, or create single-country markets to target specific regions.
Create markets for B2B company locations or groups of B2B customers grouped by region, and customize your B2B selling experience based on your negotiated contracts with B2B customers.
If you have a network of retail locations that offer different products or pricing, then you can customize those experiences with retail markets.

Create markets for the sales channels that you sell through, and customize product availability, pricing, and currency for each channel. You can group channels to share the same catalog, or give a single channel its own product catalog.
Create markets that target specific states or provinces within a country, so that you can set up different shipping options for different sub-regions. This feature is available as early access.

A market is a set of customers that you define in your store. Markets can be made up of countries or regions for cross-border sales, company locations for B2B sales, retail locations for in-person sales, or sales channels for selling across channels.
When a customer visits your store, it's determined which market they belong to, and the experience that you've configured for that market is displayed.
A submarket is a market that exists within another market. Submarkets inherit the customizations of their parent market, which means you don't need to configure every setting from scratch.
You need to have shipping rates configured for all countries and regions that you want to sell to. Markets can be activated only for countries and regions that have shipping rates.
Fixed amount discounts can be created only in your store's default currency. The discount amount is converted to your customer's currency at checkout based on current exchange rates.
Staff permissions can't be assigned per market. For example, if a staff member has the permission to view Orders, then they can view orders in all your store's markets.
Only one theme can be published at a time. You can customize your theme per market, but customizations must be applied to your published theme.
Post-purchase apps work only in your store's default currency. Post-purchase offers aren't displayed for customers in markets that use a different currency.

Only customers from countries or regions in an active market can check out. If you want to sell to customers in a country or region, then it must be included in an active market. B2B company locations, retail locations, and sales channels only need to be included in a market if you want to customize their buying experience.

To access the Markets page, a staff member needs all of the following permissions: * Home * Orders (all permissions) * Products (all permissions) * Analytics (all permissions) * Discounts (all permissions) * Catalogs (create and edit) * Store settings: manage settings, shipping and delivery, taxes and duties, domains

To accept payments in multiple currencies, you need to use Shopify Payments or Adyen as your payment processor. If you use a different payment processor, then customers in all markets pay in your store's default currency.

Per-market theme customization, such as showing different section content, banners, or layouts for different markets, requires the Advanced plan or higher. On other plans, all markets share the same theme customization.
Markets can be created for different types of customers depending on how you sell. Each market type uses a different kind of condition to define its audience.
Country or region markets are displayed to customers based on their geographic location. These markets are used for cross-border and international selling.

When a customer visits your online store, their location is determined and they're matched to the appropriate country or region market. The customer then receives the experience that you've configured for that market, including currency, language, product availability, and theme customizations. A country or region market can contain a single country or multiple countries.
Single-country markets contain one country or region. When you create a single-country market, the currency is automatically set to that country's local currency.

Multi-country markets contain more than one country or region. When you create a multi-country market, the currency customization is set to use local currencies by default. Local currencies are activated so that each country displays prices in its own currency.
A sub-region market targets a specific state or province, instead of a whole country. Use one when you want different shipping for part of a country.

Retail markets use POS locations as their condition. A retail market can target all POS locations, or specific POS locations. Retail customers are also part of a regional market based on the POS location's address, which means that a retail transaction can be associated with both a retail market and a country or region market.

You can include company locations in B2B markets in three different ways: * All company locations in all regions: Includes all company locations, regardless of where they're located. * All company locations within a region: Includes all company locations shipping to addresses in the selected regions. As you add more company locations that meet this criteria, they're automatically matched to these markets. * Specific company locations: Includes only the company locations you specify, regardless of where they're shipping to.

Channel markets use sales channels as their condition. A channel market can contain a single sales channel, or a group of channels sharing the same customizations. Channel markets let you set product availability, pricing, and currency for the specific sales channels that you sell through, such as Google & YouTube, Facebook & Instagram, or TikTok.

You can use all market types in the same store. Markets of different types can overlap, in which case the customer's experience is based on which settings are the most specific: * B2B markets are more specific than retail markets. Retail markets are more specific than country or region markets. * When a customer qualifies for markets of multiple types, the more specific market type takes priority for how your market customizations take effect. * Catalogs from all applicable markets are combined, so customers can access products from all relevant catalogs.
Country or region markets are available on all Shopify plans. There's no limit to the number of country or region markets you can create.
You can create markets from the Markets page in your Shopify admin to define where and how you sell to different customer groups.

When you create a Shopify store, the following markets are created for you automatically: * Domestic market: Your store's home country or region, as determined by your store's address and currency. This is your domestic market and represents the default customer experience. The country in your domestic market is set as your backup region by default. * International market: A curated list of countries or regions where merchants similar to you also sell. This market is inactive by default.

identifier: Create a market {#create-market}, Includes, Add condition
statement: In the Includes section, click Add condition. This condition defines which of your customers the market is displayed to: * To create a Regional market, select Regions, and then select the country or regions to create a market for. * To create a sub-region market, select Regions, open the country you want to target, and then select the states or provinces to create a market for. Learn more about sub-region markets. * To create a B2B market, select Company locations, and then select the company locations to create a market for. To limit the market to one area, use the in filter to display only company locations in a specific region or sub-region, such as a state or province. * To create a Retail market, select POS locations, and then select the retail locations to create a market for. * To create a Channel market, select Channels, and then select the sales channels to create a market for.

If you create a market as a draft, or if you don't already ship to all the countries in a new market, then the market is inactive by default. Customers in inactive markets can't complete a purchase, and receive the backup region experience when they visit your store.

Markets for a customer are automatically determined by using the following information: * When a customer first visits your store, their geographic location is determined by using their IP address, and they're matched to the appropriate market. * The customer's browser language preferences are used to determine which language to display, if you've configured multiple languages for that market. * If a customer arrives on a market-specific domain, subdomain, or subfolder (for example, yourstore.com/fr/), then they get the experience for that market. * If a customer manually chooses a different country or language by using your store's selectors, then their preference is saved and used for future visits.
You can choose whether you want to automatically or manually localize your customers. By default, automatic redirection is activated in new stores, and automatic language detection is deactivated.

A customer's shipping address determines the final experience they receive. For example, if a customer from the United States is shopping online in USD but enters a Canadian shipping address at checkout, then their experience is updated to match the Canada market, including currency and any other customizations that are applied to the Canada market.

identifier: Add or remove countries from a market
statement: You can adjust which countries or regions belong to a market as your selling strategy changes. A country or region can be included in more than one market.
If you no longer want to sell to customers in a particular market, then you can deactivate it. Deactivating a market saves all your settings, so you can reactivate it later.
Deleting a market is permanent. Deleted markets can't be recovered, and must be recreated if needed.

Your primary market is the main country or region that you sell to. It's typically your domestic market, and represents the default customer experience for your store. Review the following characteristics of the primary market: * Your primary market can contain only one country or region. * Your primary market can't be deleted. * All changes to your store's default settings apply to your primary market automatically. * Your primary market is determined by your store currency in Settings > General. For example, if your store address is in the United States but your currency is set to Canadian dollars, then your primary market is set to Canada.

Markets with subfolders configured can't be made into a primary market, because it would create broken URLs. Update the domain settings first. Markets with more than one region also can't be made primary, because primary markets are limited to one region.

Markets form a hierarchy based on their conditions: * A market with broader conditions is a parent market of a market with more specific conditions. * A market with more specific conditions is a submarket of the broader market.
If a new market is determined to be within an existing market, then it's considered a submarket.

After you delete a submarket, customers in the submarket's region receive the parent market experience instead. Other submarkets of the same parent market aren't affected. When you delete a parent market, its submarkets no longer inherit settings from it. The submarkets continue to exist, but their inherited settings revert to your store's defaults.
Product publishing rules don't apply to draft orders. You can add any product to a draft order regardless of market restrictions.

statement: Homepage banners, announcement bars, and block content can't differ between markets on the Basic or Grow plans, even if you use the Translate & Adapt app for market-specific wording for the same language.
You can assign discounts to specific B2B, country or region, and retail markets, but you can't assign discounts to specific channel markets. By default, discount codes work across all markets.
Gift cards are created and denominated in your store's default currency. You can't create gift cards in a specific market's local currency.

This backup region isn't a market. Instead, it's a setting that points to a country within one of your active markets. The customer experience for the backup region is based on the settings of the market that contains the backup region country.

The backup region must be a country that's contained within an active market. If you deactivate the market that contains your backup region country, then you need to update your backup region to a country in a different active market.
In the Backup Region section, select the region that you want to display to customers who don't match any existing market.

identifier: Backup region and the domestic market
statement: When you first create your store, your domestic market is created automatically with your home country, and the backup region is set to that same country. This means unmatched customers receive the same experience as your domestic customers, without the ability to complete a checkout.

identifier: Managed Markets changes to your store: International sales tools
statement: Incompatible countries are removed. Markets managed by Managed Markets can use only compatible currencies. Review your currency settings before you activate Managed Markets.

Review the new market created for Managed Markets. By default, this market is called Rest of World and includes all regions that are eligible for Managed Markets, but you can change your market name and remove countries and regions from the list of included regions.

Previously, markets were composed only of specific countries or regions. Markets have now been expanded, and can be used to represent specific sets of customers by creating markets and submarkets. You can group your B2B customers to create a customized store experience for each group. For each market, you can customize currency, theme, collection of taxes and duties, discounts, and pricing and product availability with catalogs.

The following changes are made to your store when you opt in: * A B2B All market is automatically created that includes all your existing companies and locations. * Catalogs aren't assigned to the B2B All market. * Your store's default products, prices, and currency are displayed to companies and company locations outside other markets that don't have an assigned catalog.

identifier: Customer experience determination in B2B with Markets
statement: The experience that a company location receives on your online store is determined by the markets that they match.

identifier: Customer experience determination in B2B with Markets
statement: A company location can match multiple markets at the same time, and which markets they match depends on the shipping address.

You can create a new market to use with B2B in your Shopify admin on the Markets page. When you create your market, ensure that you select Company locations in the Includes section. To create a functioning B2B market, you must assign company locations to the market. A B2B market without company locations won't deliver B2B pricing or experiences to your wholesale customers.

Retail markets are a type of market that are designed to support unique customizations for in-person selling with Shopify POS. With Retail markets, you can create retail-specific merchandizing strategies that are different from your online or B2B customer experiences.

You can use Markets to set your product availability, pricing, and currency for specific sales channels that you use. You can group channels together in a market, for example using the same shared product catalog for all your social channels, or you can have a single market and product catalog for one specific sales channel.

identifier: Considerations and limitations for using channel markets
statement: * When you create a channel market: * Any regions that you select for the channel market must correspond to regions that are supported by the relevant sales channel. * Any currency that you set in a customized product catalog for the channel market should be the preferred currency for the relevant sales channel. If you set a currency that's not a preferred currency for the sales channel, then a warning message is displayed. * Agentic storefronts sales channels can't be added to channel markets.

identifier: Local currency on orders and draft orders with Markets
statement: When using Markets for international sales, the local currency and pricing are determined by the market associated with the customer's order. The market that's associated with the order, as well as the taxes and duties, are determined by the shipping address of the customer.

In Shopify, a market is a group of buyers that a merchant targets with a specific buying experience. Each market is defined by conditions that determine which buyers match it. Conditions can match a buyer on signals such as where they're located, the retail location they're shopping at, or the company location they're buying for.

A channel market is a market that's scoped to a sales channel connection. Merchants use channel markets when they want channel-specific product availability, pricing, or currency for the channel's product feed. Merchants can't configure web presence, domains, or discounts for channel markets.

identifier: Considerations and limitations for using channel markets
statement: Agentic storefronts sales channels can't be added to channel markets.

identifier: Create channel markets with the GraphQL Admin API (developer changelog)
statement: Starting in API version 2026-07, the GraphQL Admin API supports channel markets. Apps can now create and update Markets that apply to one or more sales channels, then use existing catalog and market APIs to manage channel-specific product availability, pricing, and currency.

The following expansion store types are automatically eligible: * International stores: Identical brand/name and products in different languages, region, or currency. For example, abc123.com, abc123.ca, abc123.com.au. * B2B wholesale stores: Identical products as the main brand, requires user login and B2B organization association. Limit of one free B2B store per contract. * D2C stores for wholesale merchants: For merchants exclusively selling wholesale who want to create a direct-to-consumer (D2C) storefront with identical products. Limit of 1 free B2C store per contract. * Employee-only stores: Part of main business reflecting the same brand, not available to the general public. * Physical retail locations: 100% physical retail with no online transactions, identical branding, name, and products to the main brand.

statement: Shopify Plus plan organizations can have a maximum of ten stores on their contract with no additional cost: * One main store. * Nine expansion stores. * Staging stores don’t count towards the ten store limit. If you want more than ten stores, then you need to contact Shopify Support.

identifier: Setting up customer information at checkout {#customer-information}: additional address fields; Customer information settings
statement: Note Some additional address fields, such as Neighborhood, are required in certain countries and regions and are displayed automatically in the checkout form based on the country selected by the customer during checkout. The requirement for each additional address field depends on the customer's country or region and can't be changed. Learn more about additional address fields, including which fields are required for each country or region. Other than those additional address fields, the Customer information settings apply to every country and market that you sell to.

identifier: Markets (Shopify Plus plan, Growth and expansion tools on Shopify Plus)
statement: Markets Create B2B markets to sell wholesale to different regions and customize Checkout Blocks for each market. All Shopify plans include an unlimited number of country or region markets. Theme editor customization by market is available on the Advanced plan and higher. Unlimited B2B catalogs and direct catalog assignment to company locations are available only on the Shopify Plus plan.

You can use Shopify B2B on the Basic, Grow, Advanced, and Shopify Plus plans. Shopify B2B isn't available on the Starter or Retail plans. The features available to you depend on your plan. Most B2B features are available on all plans, including companies, catalogs, net payment terms, self-serve ordering, and Shopify Flow automations. Review the following key differences between plans: * B2B market catalogs: On the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans, you can assign up to 3 active catalogs across all your B2B markets. Assigning 3 catalogs to one B2B market uses the full limit. You need to remove or draft an existing assignment before you can add catalogs to another market. On the Shopify Plus plan, you can create an unlimited number of B2B market catalogs. * Direct company catalogs: On the Shopify Plus plan, you can also assign catalogs directly to specific companies and company locations for customer-level pricing. Direct catalog assignment isn't available on the Basic, Grow, or Advanced plans. * Advanced payments: Deposit requirements, partial payments, and payment requests per fulfillment are available only on the Shopify Plus plan. * Contextual experiences: Contextual checkout and storefront customization through Shopify Markets are available on the Advanced and Plus plans. To use B2B catalog features on the Basic, Grow, or Advanced plans, your store must be using new Shopify Markets.

identifier: Different Shopify plans offer different features for cross-border selling (Store setup checklist for selling in China)
statement: - Different Shopify plans offer different features for cross-border selling: - Basic: International sales tools, unlimited country or region markets, local currency pricing, B2B markets with up to 3 active catalogs assigned across all B2B markets - Grow: All Basic features plus 5 staff accounts, comprehensive reports, add carrier-calculated shipping for a monthly fee - Advanced: All Grow features plus 15 staff accounts, carrier-calculated shipping included in subscription cost - Plus: All Advanced features plus unlimited staff accounts, 9 expansion stores, unlimited B2B catalogs

identifier: Restrict access to your store or specific pages for B2B customers only {#restrict-access}
statement: By default, your B2B store is publicly accessible. Anyone can visit and browse your products and store content, including D2C customers. However, only logged-in B2B customers can access B2B-specific pricing, B2B-only products, and B2B-exclusive store content. If you operate a dedicated B2B store, then you can restrict access so that only logged-in B2B customers can view your store.

identifier: Considerations for restricting store access: blended store with B2B Markets
statement: If you operate a blended store with B2B Markets and customer accounts, then restricting access might redirect D2C customers to authentication on some pages. Test your storefront as both a B2B and D2C customer before activating this setting.

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Currency, markets, and business entities {#currency-markets-and-business-entities}, One business entity
statement: One business entity: Shopify POS transactions process in your store’s default currency. Retail markets still control catalog and price rules for your retail locations, but they don’t change the processing currency for Shopify POS when you have a single entity.
scope: Shopify POS; stores with one business entity

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Shopify plan considerations for Retail markets, Shopify POS Lite
statement: Locations that are on Shopify POS Lite use Region markets only. You assign catalogs to a Region market to control which products are available and which prices apply in that region. Your retail locations and your online store in that region use the same catalog settings.

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Shopify plan considerations for Retail markets, Region markets
statement: You can't apply different market settings to retail and online customers within the same region. Region markets apply in the same way to your online store and to retail locations in that region.

identifier: Managing fulfillment locations in shipping profiles: Note (shipping options by market)
statement: Shipping profiles and shipping rates are gradually moving to shipping options by market, a new way to manage shipping from your markets. Most stores still use shipping profiles and shipping rates, and your store keeps its current setup until it's upgraded.

identifier: Considerations before you cancel your Plus trial {#considerations}: plan limits
statement: Each Shopify subscription plan has different limits for inventory locations, and staff accounts. If you have more active markets, locations, or staff than your new plan allows, then any that exceed the new limits are deactivated automatically after you downgrade.

identifier: Shopper help hub: your guide to buying from Salla stores
statement: Salla is a Saudi technology platform that thousands of merchants use to build and run their online stores. As a shopper, you buy from the store itself, not from Salla.

identifier: Shopper help hub: your guide to buying from Salla stores
statement: The store you bought from is a legally independent business . It owns the product, sets the price and the return policy, prepares and ships your order, and handles customer service.

identifier: ❓ Did Salla sell me the product?
statement: No. The seller is the store where you placed the order, and it is the party responsible for the product, the shipping, and the return. Salla's role is limited to providing the technical platform the store runs on.

identifier: ❓ Can I buy from Salla stores from outside Saudi Arabia?
statement: That depends on the store. Each store decides which countries it ships to and which payment methods it accepts. Check the store's shipping policy page before you complete your order.

A **channel** is a place where a merchant's store sells products. Storefront websites, marketplaces like Amazon and eBay, point-of-sale systems, and marketing feeds are all sales channels. A custom channel may not fit into any one of these types.

identifier: A channel is defined by the following
statement: A channel is defined by the following: * A `name`, which is merchant-defined for internal convenience and not exposed to shoppers * A `type`, which may be one of the following: * `storefront`, * `marketing`, * `pos`, * `marketplace` * `custom` * A `platform`, which indicates the platform on which shoppers primarily use the channel

Each BigCommerce store is provisioned with one channel out of the box, intended for its first Stencil storefront. The ID of this channel is `1` for all BigCommerce stores. This channel may also be referred to as the "default channel", and it cannot be deleted.

A **site** is a website owned or controlled exclusively by the merchant, usually for hosting a storefront website. Every site will be tied to exactly one channel, but because not all sales channels are sites, channels are not required to have a site. Sites are mainly relevant to storefront-type channels, and they serve as containers for settings and objects that only apply to websites.
The first Stencil storefront of each merchant store has an ID of `1000` and is also known as the default site. It cannot be deleted.
Allowed values for a channel's `status` vary by channel `type`.
`storefront` | `prelaunch`, `active`, `inactive`, `archived`, `deleted`
`marketing`, `marketplace`, `pos` | `connected`, `disconnected`, `archived`, `deleted`

You can restore a Channel with `deleted` status within **90 days** after deletion by contacting the BigCommerce support team. After the 90-days grace period is over, the Channel `status` will become `terminated`.
The `terminated` status is read-only. Channels with a `status` of `terminated` **cannot** be restored.

Multi-Storefront (MSF) allows you to use a single BigCommerce “store” to power multiple “storefronts”. Each of these storefronts can have its own unique domain, theme, categories, web pages, social media links, price lists, email templates, and more. The settings and data for each of these storefronts are managed from one BigCommerce control panel.

Depending on your business model, multi-storefront may work for some merchants as a multi-region or cross-border solution. However, some store functions are global and are shared across storefronts, such as the built-in blog. Additionally, even though the same product can be assigned to different storefronts, product attributes (like description and name) cannot be overridden into a different language without customization. Stores on a Performance plan will have access to additional product localization fields.
Multi-storefront can be useful for merchants who have multiple brands or who serve multiple segments like B2C, B2B, retail, and wholesale segments.
All apps are designed to work at a store level and are installed at the store level. Every app should work on the default storefront that is provisioned when a new store is created.

Additional storefronts can help you to tailor the shopping experience for different audiences or strategies, such as: Localization — Create region-specific storefronts to accommodate different languages, currencies, or cultural preferences. Brand Differentiation — Launch unique storefronts for individual brands under your business umbrella. Customer Segmentation — Serve distinct customer cohorts, such as B2B, wholesale, or VIP customers, with dedicated storefronts.
